title: Mech physical classification, Frame equipment, and student vehicle tiers
summary: Classify mech art by movement method/size/mounting capability to drive real Frame build variety; reflavor real SF2E items into Frame-specific and vehicle-specific equipment (named via real military/civil vehicle classes); lock in a grid-size-to-power-tier convention; a literal world map asset already exists.
description:
The generated mech artwork turned out with real variety in size and equipment loadout, and the user wants to lean into that rather than normalize it away. Proposed classification axes: movement method (e.g. tracked feet = faster; four legs = harder to knock over/more stable), and physical form as a gate on what equipment can be mounted (large cannon mounts allow certain heavy weapon classes; hands allow carrying and swapping a wider range of equipment on shorter notice than a fixed mount). The user will help classify the actual mech images once shared.

Equipment plan: take real SF2E items and produce reflavored, campaign-unique versions specifically for Frame use — not generic reskins, bespoke to this campaign. Separately, produce equipment for students in vehicles, explicitly named using real military/civil vehicle classes (IFV, APC, recon vehicles, helicopters, etc.) so vehicle players have their own real gear-choice axis (e.g. better-armored-but-slower vs. faster-but-more-fragile, with fast vehicles specifically enabling covering large map distances quickly). This is the concrete mechanism meant to let vehicles keep pace with Frames in large-scale impact. (As captured this served the goal that non-piloting 'ground-role' students not be second-line; the ground roles were cut on 2026-09-20, and every player is now in a Frame or a vehicle for large-scale combat.)

Grid-size convention (concrete, ready to use): larger Frames occupy a 2x2 grid footprint instead of the SF2E-standard 1x1; smaller mechs can use ordinary SF2E creature sizes to appear on the map at 1x1; a 3x3 footprint is reserved specifically for extremely high-end antagonists (climactic/boss-tier Claimants); a student on foot gets the smallest available size, to visually sell the size gap next to Frames.

A literal world map asset has already been produced: a heavily zoomed-out view of the city being defended, including a large amount of surrounding ocean and inland mountains/plains — meant for the satellite-view mech-scale combat concept already noted as an evolving mechanics thread.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump.
